items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: Santo came in my band. Santa Picora, you know him, don't you?

ctx.x: scene. So the theater's one place you'd hear. Where else did you?

Now, now, I took you off from the theater, which was strictly long here, until I went in there, and when I started playing that Charno We Own A Lot To You, with the mute, the house came down, it became a feature. So the Palace had to do the same thing. And they had better jazz men than we had, and Melvin Berry, who was my trombonist tonight. You see, the boys used to double. Now, Santa Picora, was my, when Berry went to California, Berry got a big job out there. Santo came in my band. Santa Picora, you know him,…
helped their music. Were they calling it jazz at that time?

items.title: Santo Pecora Interview, 1972-11-09
items.q: Oh, yeah, well, I played the Groomall Hotel, at Roosevelt Hotel now, with Johnny Deidre, I only got $20.

ctx.x: Well, that was good money for a place like that.
Oh, yeah, well, I played the Groomall Hotel, at Roosevelt Hotel now, with Johnny Deidre, I only got $20. I think it was from $10.30 to $1, $20 a week. But we made tips. We had made with.
This is the third reel, Santa. Yeah. We're set, we're going.
